name: AMP1
title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
authors: Chen Chen, …, Matthias Müller, Vladlen Koltun
interface: Python in a persistent interpreter; SDK for sensing, a segmented scene model, and timed TCP waypoints (harness does IK + limit checks)
trials: 108 real trials over 12 tasks × 3 robots

speed.latency: avg 34.8 model calls per RoboLab episode

summary: Reference harness that runs unchanged on single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation with no grasp/push/place skills. Zero-shot 85.6% on RoboLab-120 (vs 49.2% leading VLA, 42.9% leading WAM); 104/108 real-world successes. AMP1+ adds a persistent notes/code memory that lifts RoboDojo from 26.4% to 84.1% after practice.
caveats: Authors: 'AMPs are not yet practical, as the robot spends much of each episode waiting for the model.' Quasi-static scenes only; no mid-trajectory revision. Proposed fix is to distill AMP experience into fast local controllers.
milestone: A generalist model beats specialist VLAs and WAMs by a wide margin in the real world as well as in sim.

name: Astranomy
title: Astranomy: An Empirical Study of GPT-6 Astra as a Native Robot Policy
authors: Jenai Xuning Yang, Ashna Khetan, Shun Zhang
interface: Three roles: Direct (EEF / joint / B-spline chunks per API call), Agentic (persistent Codex session with tools), Orchestrated (reviews or overrides Cosmos3-Nano-Policy proposals)
trials: 120 tasks × 5 seeds

speed.latency: Direct 18.56 s/call; Agentic 13.37 s; π0.5 46.96 ms

summary: Zero-shot on RoboLab-120: Agentic 74.8%, Orchestrated 66.5%, Direct (EEF) 66.3%, against Cosmos3-Nano-Policy 36.8% and π0.5 28.0%. Ablations: the action space and the geometry in the prompt matter hugely for Direct (19.3% → 72.7% with gripper/camera geometry) but barely for Agentic.
caveats: Sim only; 5 episodes per task (authors flag this); no arXiv yet. Putting Astra on top of a weak System 1 (Orchestrated) did not beat Astra alone.
milestone: First controlled study comparing the three roles a frontier model can take: direct, agentic, and orchestrator.

name: ATLAS
title: ATLAS: Agentic Harness for Whole-Body Intelligence from Human Video
authors: Junli Ren, Kaixiang Yao, …, Ran Tian
venue: Best Demo, CoRL 2026 Agentic Robotics Workshop
interface: Agent writes a task spec once from 1 human video + 1 prompt; harness edits the end-effector reach; frozen ScaleBFM whole-body tracker (System 0) follows the edited motion; a fast learner adds a residual
trials: 38 real attempts (trash pickup)
summary: Humanoid whole-body tasks from one human video, no robot demos or task-specific sim training. Real trash pickup goes from 0% to 88% (last 8 attempts) within 38 attempts. In Isaac Lab, online model-based RL reaches 83% apple lift vs 58% bias estimator / 13% model-free RL / 4% no learner.
caveats: Project page only (no paper link yet); the VLM is not named. Date is from the announcement post.
milestone: Clearest example of a frontier agent steering a frozen System 0 rather than replacing it.

name: OpenRUA
title: OpenRUA: Robot-Use Agents Are Zero-Shot Visuomotor Policies
interface: Zero-abstraction: terminal access to native ROS 2 plus its docs only; perception becomes file I/O, manipulation becomes coding
summary: An off-the-shelf coding agent, with no bespoke primitives, reaches 99.0% on CaP-Bench and 87.0% on LIBERO-PRO. Emergent behaviour: the agent writes its own metric-perception code in 96.8% of episodes and its own motion-control clients in 95.9%.
caveats: Secondary critiques note the simulator is paused while the agent thinks, episodes take ~100 turns, and baselines are copied from original papers. The OpenRUA team also published retests of RoboDojo leaderboard entries (see Critiques).
milestone: Showed that bespoke harness engineering may be unnecessary: native ROS 2 is enough.

name: CaP-X
title: CaP-X: A Framework for Benchmarking and Improving Coding Agents for Robot Manipulation
models: 12 models incl. Gemini 3 Pro, GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.5
interface: Programs that compose perception and control primitives at varying abstraction levels (CaP-Gym)
summary: CaP-Gym environment + CaP-Bench. Finding: performance rises with human-crafted abstractions and falls as they are removed, but scaling agentic test-time compute (multi-turn, execution feedback, visual differencing, skill synthesis) closes much of the gap. Introduces training-free CaP-Agent0 and CaP-RL (RL with verifiable rewards, sim→real).
caveats: Authors propose a hybrid in which agents handle logic and recovery while VLAs handle fine motor control.
milestone: The shared benchmark that made agent-vs-VLA comparisons routine.

name: FAEA
title: Demonstration-Free Robotic Control via LLM Agents
interface: Software-engineering agent loop applied unchanged to manipulation
summary: Frontier Agent as Embodied Agent: 84.9% LIBERO, 85.7% ManiSkill3, 96% MetaWorld, approaching VLAs trained on fewer than 100 demos per task, with zero demonstrations. One round of human feedback raises LIBERO to 88.2%.
caveats: Uses privileged environment state. Authors scope the claim to 'tasks dominated by deliberative, task-level planning'.
milestone: Early evidence that unmodified coding-agent infrastructure transfers to manipulation.

name: ALRM
title: ALRM: Agentic LLM for Robotic Manipulation
authors: Vitor Gaboardi dos Santos et al.
models: 10 LLMs; best closed: Claude-4.1-Opus; best open: Falcon-H1-7B
interface: ReAct loop in two modes: Code-as-Policy (writes control code) and Tool-as-Policy (iterative tool calls)
summary: Agentic framework plus a 56-task simulation benchmark with linguistically varied instructions. Claude-4.1-Opus is the top closed model under both modes.

name: AGP
title: Agent as Policy for Robotic Manipulation
interface: Agent reads visual evidence, writes programs, issues motion commands, revises on physical outcomes
summary: A general agent drives a physical robot through the whole task, including dynamic and deformable ones (dice flipping, targeted throwing, bimanual towel folding, assembly from human video). At least 80% success on 7 of 8 task configurations. Reusing saved procedures shortens execution over repeated trials.

name: Show-Harness
title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
interface: Discrete semantic action units that embodiment-specific interpreters ground deterministically; the VLM stays responsible for fine-grained physical decisions
summary: Argues the right interface unlocks VLM capability without extra capacity: zero-shot control with closed frontier VLMs, and small open VLMs adapted with a few GPU-hours. GUMI extends the same action space to GUI-based demonstration collection.

name: GPT-Policy
title: In-Context Robot Learning with VLM Agents
interface: Context compiler → VLM proposes robot-tool actions → constrained controller verifies and executes
summary: In-context robot learning without gradient updates. Human video demos help even without action labels; aligned action references help further on contact-sensitive tasks.

name: EMERGE-Policy
title: EMERGE-Policy: A Robot Mind Emerges Beyond a Single Policy
interface: Graph of a main agent plus sub-agents (perception, monitoring, verification, memory); heterogeneous model backends exposed as Operational / Imagination / Evaluation skills
summary: Treats models, including action models, as skills called inside a multi-agent orchestration, with verification and branch-stack recovery. No additional fine-tuning.

name: GTA-2
title: GTA-2: A Multi-VLM Framework for Synthesizing Robot Manipulation Skills via Grounded Task Axes
interface: Four VLM agents build task-axis skills: keypoints/axes, controller compositions, scene parameters
trials: 14 real tasks
summary: Zero-shot 73.9% average on 14 real-robot tasks, 31.4 pp above the strongest baseline (π0.5 and two Code-as-Policies variants); targeted human feedback raises it to 90.7%.

name: RAPID
title: RAPID: Robot Agentic Programming from Demonstrations
interface: Object-centric relational programs whose primitives are trajectory-optimization programs
summary: From one visual human demonstration, infers a testable spec, primitives, and an environment, then generates, verifies, and refines robot programs. Covers 8 contact-rich nonprehensile tasks (sim and a real Franka) plus LIBERO-Pro.

name: Harness VLA
title: Harness VLA: Steering Frozen VLAs into Reliable Manipulation Primitives via Memory-Guided Agents
interface: Frozen VLA exposed as a retryable contact-rich primitive, plus analytic primitives for grounding, staging, transport, and release
summary: Keeps a learned System 1 only for the local contact-rich phases and lifts everything else to the planner. +38.6 pp on LIBERO-Pro and +25.4 pp on RoboCasa365 over the strongest baselines; 58.4% on RoboTwin C2R; real dual-Franka demos.
caveats: AMP1 notes that orchestration methods like this are capped by the reliability of the VLA they delegate to.
milestone: The canonical 'keep System 1 for contact' design.

name: HarnessPAI
title: HarnessPAI: An Evolving Harness for Physical AI
interface: Code as the evolvable interface that organizes underlying action primitives: open-loop program within a rollout, closed-loop evolution across rollouts
summary: Argues that the action-model training recipe erodes perception and reasoning. Works across arms, household robots, a robot vacuum, and a legged agent. The converged programs also become cheap expert data for fine-tuning VLAs and WAMs.

name: Gemini Robotics 1.5
title: Gemini Robotics 1.5: Pushing the Frontier of Generalist Robots with Advanced Embodied Reasoning, Thinking, and Motion Transfer
interface: ER model sends step-level natural-language instructions to a 'thinking' VLA
summary: ER 1.5 as orchestrator cuts planning failures from 25.5% (generic Gemini 2.5 Flash orchestrator) to 9%. The VLA writes language thinking traces before acting.
caveats: Vendor evaluation.

name: Gemini Robotics 2
title: Gemini Robotics 2 brings whole-body intelligence to robots
interface: ER 2 plans, monitors, and coordinates; the VLA emits motor commands; an on-device VLA runs locally
summary: Whole-body humanoid control. Reported success includes 74.2% general pick-and-place and 89.6% precise insertion on Franka Duo, and 36–92% on multi-finger tasks, which the page says 'remains challenging'. On-Device 2 adapts to new bi-arms with fewer than 200 examples.
caveats: Vendor blog; numbers not independently reproduced.

name: Claude on robotics
title: How Claude performs on robotics tasks
authors: Shmuel Berman, Michael Ilie, Jia Deng, Daniel Freeman
interface: Four interfaces compared: direct torques/commands, programmatic controller, model-designed RL, high-level steering of a gait or VLA (MolmoAct)
trials: 35 per cell (200 for LIBERO-40)

speed.latency: ≈0.2–0.4 Hz non-reasoning calls vs ≈83 Hz needed for quadruped control

summary: 'Interface matters as much as the model.' Direct joint control mostly fails: best LIBERO full-task success is 5.5%, and no model stands a collapsed G1 up. Supervising pretrained controllers works far better. However, every model did worse supervising MolmoAct than MolmoAct alone on its own tasks, while beating it on novel tasks.
caveats: Simulator paused between calls (best-case capability); prompts not tuned per model.
milestone: Direct evidence that a frontier model on top of System 1 can hurt in-distribution and help out-of-distribution.

name: Bitter Lesson → Robotics
title: The Bitter Lesson Comes to Robotics
models: 9 frontier multimodal LMs at multiple effort / service tiers
interface: Direct end-effector pose commands
trials: 6 RoboDojo tasks on physical hardware

speed.latency: best execution rate improved 4.4× (Jul–Oct 2026)

summary: First broad comparison of frontier LMs on a common real-hardware manipulation suite. Models can directly control real arms but are not yet precise or efficient enough to finish within a practical action budget. Performance doubling time of 53.9 days over July–October 2026.
caveats: Short window (4 months) and 6 tasks: a weak basis for extrapolation.
milestone: First 'scaling-trend' measurement for frontier models as robot policies.

name: LLM as Policy on RoboDojo
title: An Unexpected Robot Policy: Early Evaluations of GPT-6 Astra on RoboDojo and Beyond
interface: LLM as policy with shared post-processing
trials: 42 tasks × 50 episodes (Astra, GPT-5.5); 10 (DeepSeek)
summary: Frames the question in System 1 / System 2 terms. Astra: 22.48% success, Score 28.97, ranking above all 40 public policies; GPT-5.5 0.88% and DeepSeek-Flash 1.92%. Capability is sharply polarized: good at semantic generalization, poor at precision, dynamic control, and bimanual coordination. One-shot demos give no aggregate gain.
milestone: First time an LLM topped a public robot-policy leaderboard.

name: Frontier models on LIBERO-10
title: From Reasoning to Action: Benchmarking Frontier AI Models on LIBERO-10 Robot Manipulation Tasks
interface: Structured tool calls specifying target EEF poses and gripper commands
trials: 18 configurations, 1,800 episodes
summary: Best is Astra at 44%, then Gemini-4 Argon at 43%. More reasoning effort generally helps, at extra cost. Models do well on placement and struggle with precise spatial arrangement and multi-step interaction.

name: ASPIRE
title: ASPIRE: Agentic /Skills Discovery for Robotics
interface: Code-as-policy with closed-loop execution traces, a growing skill library, and evolutionary program search
summary: Continual code-as-policy learning. With Claude Opus 5.5 it nearly saturates benchmarks: 99% on all 80 LIBERO-Pro tasks, 100% on representative Robosuite and BEHAVIOR-1K tasks. Performance scales with the underlying frontier model. Skills found in sim transfer to the real robot.

name: ENPIRE
title: ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World
interface: Harness with Environment (auto reset and verify), Policy Improvement, Rollout (robot fleet), and Evolution (agent edits training code) modules
summary: The frontier agent does not act as the policy; it is the researcher that trains a fast System 1. It reaches 99% success on dexterous real tasks (pin-box organizing, zip-tie fastening, tool use).
milestone: An alternative answer: the frontier model builds System 1 instead of replacing it.

name: SEAR
title: SEAR: Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics
interface: Three modes on the same tools: code-as-policy, agent-as-policy (live in the loop), and auto-research (fine-tunes a VLA)
trials: 330 sim + 5 physical tasks; >4 years of agent runtime
summary: Asks 'is the agent really learning, or just trying more often?'. Controls separate retained experience from re-rolls, privileged state, budget, and luck. Control code and shared routines transfer; task-specific solutions don't. Models differ in whether they evolve best acting live or writing code. A text-only model keeps pace with a multimodal one.
caveats: Real-robot gap between agent-designed practice and novel human-designed scenes.

name: RACaP
title: RACaP: Agentic Reasoning, Acting, and Coding as Policies for Evolvable Robot Learning
interface: Coding moved offline into evolution; at deployment a ReAct loop calls frozen typed Policy APIs

speed.latency: 13.2× per-decision speedup after distillation; physical calls 16 → 4

summary: 54.4% LIBERO-90, 45.0% zero-shot LIBERO-PRO, 46.0% LIBERO-Long (CaP baselines ≤4% on long-horizon). Rejection-sampled fine-tuning distills GPT-5.6 ReAct decisions into an 8B open model.
milestone: One of the first concrete distillations of a frontier-agent policy into a small on-robot model.

name: uni-robot-agent
title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
interface: Unified harness for open-weight models that supports further training
trials: 19 real-world tasks
summary: An out-of-the-box open-weight model scores 31.39 on RoboDojo without privileged inputs, above the published GPT-6 Astra-RoboProbe 28.97. Links effective robot use to four general capabilities.

name: Helix
title: Helix: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Generalist Humanoid Control
interface: S2 compresses its understanding into a single latent vector, projected into S1's token space; trained end to end

speed.latency: S2 7–9 Hz, S1 200 Hz, each on its own onboard embedded GPU

summary: The canonical System 1 / System 2 split in production: a slow onboard VLM writes a latent that a 200 Hz visuomotor policy consumes asynchronously.
milestone: Popularized the 'System 1 / System 2' framing for robot foundation models.

name: GR00T N1
title: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
interface: VLM latent features feed a flow-matching DiT action head

speed.latency: VLM ≈10 Hz, action module ≈120 Hz

summary: Open-weight dual-system humanoid foundation model.

name: π0.5
title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
interface: One model predicts a language subtask, then an action chunk conditioned on it

speed.latency: 46.96 ms per call (as measured in Astranomy)

summary: Co-trained on heterogeneous robot, web, and high-level semantic data. It is the most common VLA baseline in the agentic-policy papers above.

name: Hi Robot
title: Hi Robot: Open-Ended Instruction Following with Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Models
interface: High-level VLM emits language commands to a low-level VLA
summary: Hierarchical VLA with a language interface between the reasoning and action levels.

name: Fast-in-Slow
title: Fast-in-Slow: A Dual-System Foundation Model Unifying Fast Manipulation within Slow Reasoning
interface: System 1 is the final transformer blocks of the same VLM

speed.latency: 117.7 Hz control; best System 2 : System 1 ratio 1:4

summary: Puts System 1 inside the VLM instead of in a separate head.

name: RationalVLA
title: RationalVLA: A Rational Vision-Language-Action Model with Dual System
summary: Dual-system VLA variant.

name: Dual-Process Atomic Skills
title: Dual-Process Atomic Skill Learning: Decoupling Semantic Reasoning and Real-Time Control
interface: Slow planner and fast executor inside one model, run asynchronously
summary: Asynchronous slow-planner / fast-executor in a unified model.

name: τ0-VLA
title: τ0-VLA: a Hierarchical Robot Foundation Model with World-Model-Guided Test-Time Computation
interface: Background worker refreshes the subtask about once per second; the control loop reads the cached subtask

speed.latency: planner ≈1 Hz; control ≈30 Hz action chunks

summary: A reference design for asynchronous serving: a slow planner never blocks the control loop.

name: LoHo-Manip
title: Long-Horizon Manipulation via Trace-Conditioned VLA Planning
interface: Task-manager VLM issues a subtask and visual trace once every 100 executor steps
summary: Hierarchical planner over a trace-conditioned VLA.

name: Knowledge Insulation
title: Knowledge Insulating Vision-Language-Action Models: Train Fast, Run Fast, Generalize Better
interface: Stop-gradient from the continuous action expert into the VLM; the backbone trains on discretized-action tokens plus VL data
summary: Shows that action-expert gradients damage the VLM backbone. Key evidence that fusing System 1 into System 2 has a cost, which is the reverse of 'the LLM overwhelms System 1'.

name: Actions as Language
title: Actions as Language: Fine-Tuning VLMs into VLAs Without Catastrophic Forgetting
interface: Low-level actions expressed in natural language
summary: Attributes forgetting to distribution mismatch and avoids it by expressing actions as language, with no need for internet-scale co-training.

name: TwinBrainVLA
title: TwinBrainVLA: Unleashing the Potential of Generalist VLMs for Embodied Tasks via Asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers
interface: A frozen generalist 'left brain' preserved next to a trainable embodied branch
summary: Keeps the generalist VLM frozen to protect its semantics while a second branch learns action.

name: Representation Anchoring
title: Generalizable VLA Finetuning via Representation Anchoring and Language-Action Alignment
interface: Distills hidden states from a frozen VLM copy into the trainable backbone
summary: Another fix for VLM forgetting during VLA fine-tuning.

name: InstructVLA
title: InstructVLA: Vision-Language-Action Instruction Tuning from Understanding to Manipulation
summary: VL instruction tuning to keep understanding while learning manipulation.

name: Gemini Robotics
title: Gemini Robotics: Bringing AI into the Physical World
summary: The first Gemini Robotics VLA and embodied-reasoning model release.

name: RoboLab
title: RoboLab: A High-Fidelity Simulation Benchmark for Analysis of Task Generalist Policies
summary: High-fidelity simulation benchmark with human- and LLM-authored scenes. Its 120-task suite (RoboLab-120) is where AMP1 and Astranomy report head-to-head numbers against VLAs and WAMs.
caveats: AMP1 reports that many RoboLab failures come from object geometry/mass defeating standard grasps or from a flaky verifier.

name: RoboDojo
title: RoboDojo: A Unified Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Comprehensive Evaluation of Generalist Robot Manipulation Policies
trials: official 50 episodes per task
summary: 42 sim + 18 real tasks across generalization, memory, precision, long horizon, and open-vocabulary instruction following. Public leaderboard on which LLM-as-policy entries now compete with VLAs.
caveats: See the OpenRUA retest under Critiques: some leaderboard entries changed step limits or relied on the built-in success checker.

name: LIBERO-PRO
title: LIBERO-PRO: Towards Robust and Fair Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Models Beyond Memorization
summary: Perturbed LIBERO built to defeat memorization. Agentic methods report large gains over VLAs here (CaP-X, OpenRUA, ASPIRE, RACaP, AMP1).
caveats: Papers use different LIBERO-PRO conditions and subsets, so numbers are not always comparable.

name: Butter-Bench
title: Butter-Bench: Evaluating LLM Controlled Robots for Practical Intelligence
interface: Evaluates only the LLM layer of an LLM + VLA stack
summary: Best LLM 40% vs mean human 95%. Weakest areas are multi-step spatial planning and social understanding. Embodied-reasoning fine-tuned LLMs did not improve.

name: AA-Robotics
title: AA-Robotics (research preview)
interface: Coding-agent harnesses (Codex / Claude Code / Antigravity) with an HTTP API to a 6-axis arm
trials: 8 tabletop tasks; trials per task not stated

speed.latency: ≈30 min per task vs ≈20 s for a human
speed.cost: cheapest model ≈10× a human's hourly wage

summary: Independent real-arm leaderboard. Scores out of 100: Astra 69.4, Sol 64.6, Argon 55.3, Opus 5.5 48.8, Fable 5.1 46.3.
caveats: No VLA baseline. The authors say frontier models are not yet suited to production robotics on their own.

name: Robocurve Astra eval
title: GPT-6 Astra vs Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 on bimanual YAM arms
interface: Inspect Robots `agent` policy; 3 cameras + proprioception; 20-call budget
trials: 20 per task

speed.latency: ≈2.5 min/run (Astra, bowl task)

summary: Block-into-bowl: Astra 19/20, Fable 5.1 8/20, Fable 5 1/20. Puzzle-into-groove: Astra 2/20, Fable 5.1 2/20, Fable 5 0/20. Coarse placement is solved; precise insertion is not.
caveats: Different rigs and days across models; graders knew which model was running.

name: ERIQ
title: Unified Embodied VLM Reasoning with Robotic Action via Autoregressive Discretized Pre-training
summary: Introduces ERIQ, 6K+ QA pairs separating embodied reasoning from motor control. Reports a strong correlation between embodied-reasoning score and end-to-end VLA generalization.

name: RoboDojo leaderboard retest
title: OpenRUA team retest of RoboDojo leaderboard entries (Huxiu / AI Dancer report)
summary: Reports retests of Astra-based RoboDojo entries. RoboDawn raised the step cap to 10^9 (success falls 47.1% → 1.0% under the original limit). RoboICL drops 83.2 → 63.5 when the agent must declare 'done' itself instead of the built-in checker ending the episode. HexaShell's learned skill mostly memorized one task.
caveats: Secondary Chinese-language report; find the primary OpenRUA retest before citing. Astranomy's numbers were not part of the retest.
milestone: Benchmark-integrity wake-up call for LLM-as-policy leaderboards.

name: 'Astra is shockingly good at robotics'
title: OpenAI's Astra model is shockingly good at robotics
summary: Astra briefly topped RoboDojo but is too slow for most tasks. Expects LLMs to become high-level orchestrators rather than replace VLAs, because robots need onboard models and Astra lacks dexterity. Written before AMP1, which partly contests it.

name: Robotics' New Era After Astra
title: Robotics' New Era After Astra
summary: Working hypothesis: System 2 and much of System 1 merge into frontier models, while a small embodiment-specific 'System 0' reflex controller remains. Calls this robotics' 'GPT-3 moment' and doubts the value of standalone robot foundation models.
caveats: Industry commentary; partly relies on unverified sources.

name: Robot-Use Agents
title: Robot-Use Agents
summary: General agents as 'puppeteers' that use robots as tools through existing sensor/actuator interfaces, updated centrally, versus slowly engineered on-device policies. Concedes LLM-controlled robots are 'still far less performant than dedicated solutions'.
milestone: Named and framed the 'robot-use agent' paradigm.

name: Towards Agentic Robots
title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
summary: Unified survey tracing the path from VLAs, world models, and WAMs to agentic robot systems.

name: Multimodal Embodied Agents survey
title: Survey on Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
summary: Asks what changes when a multimodal agent moves from computer-use to robot-use; organized around perceive, anticipate, plan, act, and verify.

name: From Planner to Policy
title: From Planner to Policy: a survey of large language models for robot control
summary: Organizes ~220 systems by action interface: abstraction level, representation, composition operator, invocation timing. A useful taxonomy for the System 2 → System 1 contract.
caveats: No arXiv link yet; date taken from the repo creation month.

name: VLA life-cycle survey
title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment
summary: Covers hierarchical-VLA interfaces (latents vs subtask / 2D path / language) and multi-rate execution.

name: Efficient VLA survey
title: A Survey on Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Catalogs asynchronous decoupling (Fast ECoT, SmolVLA) and other speed techniques. These are the toolbox for closing the frontier-model latency gap.

name: Toward Unified Robot Learning
title: Toward Unified Robot Learning: Bridging Representation, Vision-Language-Action, and World Models
summary: Flags inference latency of large backbones generating subgoals as a bottleneck in hierarchical VLAs.

name: SayCan
title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
interface: LLM scores candidate skills; learned value functions ground feasibility
summary: The original 'LLM picks from a learned skill library' design.

name: Inner Monologue
title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models
interface: Closed-loop language feedback (success detection, scene description) to an LLM planner
summary: Closed-loop feedback for LLM planners, the ancestor of today's observe-and-repair agent loops.

name: Code as Policies
title: Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control
interface: LLM writes policy code over perception and control APIs
summary: Direct ancestor of CaP-X, OpenRUA, and AMP1.
milestone: Introduced code as the interface between an LLM and a robot.

name: ProgPrompt
title: ProgPrompt: Generating Situated Robot Task Plans using Large Language Models
interface: Program-like prompts listing available actions and objects
summary: Programmatic prompting for situated task plans.

name: VoxPoser
title: VoxPoser: Composable 3D Value Maps for Robotic Manipulation with Language Models
interface: LLM writes code that composes 3D value maps; a motion planner synthesizes trajectories
summary: Zero-shot trajectory synthesis from LLM-composed value maps, with no learned System 1.

name: Reins
title: Reins: Frontier Multimodal Models Driving Real Robot Arms on Long-Horizon Tasks, Zero-Shot
interface: 3D perception tools plus atomic actions that report contact and grip; actions chained in one call with per-step conditions; a second 'narrator' instance watches the cameras continuously
trials: 5 real long-horizon tasks (dual-arm)
summary: Targets the 'blind while the arm moves and while it thinks' problem. GPT-6.1 Sol succeeds in 88% of real episodes with no task-specific code; without the harness it fails every shell game and takes 8× as long. Three frontier models perform alike but differ in tracking a scene that changes while the actor thinks. Also builds a sim-ready twin of the scene for continual learning.
caveats: Code to be released on publication.

name: JustRUA
title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
interface: Controlled ablation of harness, action interface, experience reuse, and scene geometry on the official L3 harness
summary: Takes apart why RoboDojo robot-use-agent scores rose so fast. Most of the gain comes from a lean harness with full episode history and early motion stops, plus scene geometry (even depth predicted from RGB). Experience reuse 'is not a free lunch'. With no learned policy, self-improvement, or task tuning: Score 29.7 → 50.3.
milestone: First controlled ablation showing which harness choices actually produce robot-use-agent gains.

name: PEAR / RURL
title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
interface: No harness: observe → chain of thought → next end-effector pose, like a computer-use agent
summary: Robot-use RL (RURL) entirely in simulation, no demos, mirroring how frontier models learn computer use. LIBERO rises from 1.6% to 74.4% (near GPT-6 Astra / GPT-6.1 Sol at max effort), with 60% on a real dual-arm robot (base model 0%). On LIBERO-Pro new-task-in-familiar-scene: 57.4% vs π0.5 0.75%. No measurable loss on 9 general reasoning, coding, and vision benchmarks.
milestone: Robot use as an ordinary foundation-model post-training skill, with no general-capability regression.

name: ACE-CaP-0
title: ACE-CaP-0: Real-World Code-as-Policies in the Era of Experience
interface: Agent develops programs with Demonstrations on Request and Simulation on Demand, then freezes them; runtime has no model in the loop
trials: 240 real trials over 8 tasks

speed.latency: 0.97–2.27 min mean task time; no model calls at runtime

summary: Moves the frontier model's reasoning to development time: frozen programs reach 92.1% (221/240) on 8 real tasks including bimanual ones, with no human or agent in the loop at runtime.

name: InteractVLA
title: InteractVLA: Turning VLAs into Interactive Tools for Agentic Robotic Manipulation
interface: Two-way geometric interface: agent-specified EEF targets steer a flow-based VLA via test-time gradient guidance; generated action chunks and reprojections are shown back to the agent
summary: Instead of treating the VLA as an opaque language-only primitive, makes System 1 geometrically steerable and inspectable by the agent. Reports 99.4% LIBERO-Plus, 48.62% RoboDojo, and 89.4% RoboCasa365, with recursive self-improvement.
milestone: A richer System 2 → System 1 contract: geometric steering instead of language commands.

name: LEASH / RoboRisk
title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
interface: Task, action, and commit gates reviewed by a decision model sharing one safety policy
trials: 92 sim + 13 physical tasks
summary: RoboRisk benchmark covers task refusal, plan repair, execution-time hazards, injection, and sequential memory, all closed-loop. All six frontier models 'generally show high harm rates'. The LEASH harness cuts harm across all six while largely preserving task completion.

name: Envisioning Agentic Robotics
title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
summary: Position and roadmap paper. Argues that 'Embodied System 2' (a foundation model plus an embodied harness) is the decision core of agentic robotics. Proposes an evaluation framework covering both model capability and closed-loop system performance, plus a roadmap toward sustained autonomy.

name: DASH
title: Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids (DASH): Latency-Agnostic Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models for Humanoid Manipulation
interface: System 2 VLM and System 1 flow-matching head as concurrent processes over LCM; System 1 fuses stale semantics with fresh vision from its own encoder

speed.latency: holds 20 Hz from 0.8B to 8B backbones (synchronous: 9.7 → 4.1 Hz)

summary: Makes the control rate independent of backbone size, which is exactly what a much larger (frontier-scale) System 2 would need. Training deliberately exposes System 1 to stale System 2 output. Higher success than the synchronous pipeline at every size and on a real dexterous humanoid.

name: H2E
title: What Can a VLA Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Embodied Navigation
interface: Successful LLM-planner + frozen-VLA sessions relabelled as VLA actions for the original task, then distilled into the VLA alone

speed.latency: distilled VLA runs 3.7× faster with zero LLM tokens

summary: Harness-to-Executor distillation folds the System 2 agent back into System 1. +15.6% (REVERIE-CE) and +11.1% (NavRAG-CE) for an 8B VLA. The student exceeds its agent teacher on unseen episodes.
caveats: Navigation, not manipulation.

name: AgentRoboCritic
title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
interface: Policy emits low-level numerical targets (EEF poses, joints, gripper) plus a local-intent note per action; a VLM critic labels each action's outcome and failure mode against that intent
judged_by: each benchmark's official grader (episodes); GPT-6 Astra as critic (actions), checked on a 400-action human-annotated set
trials: 12 benchmarks; 12,163 failed actions analysed; 12,844-action annotated dataset

speed.latency: median decision 31.9 s for GPT-6 Astra vs 0.11 s for π0.5 (74 matched tasks)

summary: Action-level analysis of GPT-6 Astra on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. '49.8% of all successful episodes contain at least one local failure'; '38.9% of the analyzed failures are recovered within 10 actions and 57.7% by the end of the episode'. Grasp and Alignment are the bottlenecks, while Choice errors are 0.2% of failed actions. A fine-tuned Muse-Glimmer-30B critic's failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%.
caveats: Authors: agents 'struggle to resolve millimeter-scale mating tolerances and angular alignment from vision alone'; only about one in three Alignment and Effect failures are recovered. Same model serves as policy and critic (self-preference tested in an appendix). 5 of 12 benchmarks reuse released traces rather than new rollouts.

name: ForceHarness
title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
interface: One tool call per turn picking a self-terminating force primitive (move_until_contact, push, insert, screw, …) run by admittance control on the stock impedance controller; a physics translation layer returns mass, friction, contact height with uncertainty
judged_by: human operator (real); ForceBench public evaluator; HiddenPhys code check on final state
trials: real: 6 tasks × 10 episodes per condition; ForceBench 8 tasks × 10; HiddenPhys 7 tasks × 20 seeds

speed.latency: 'Model queries add seconds between primitives'
speed.cost: cuts Astra's cost per episode by 45% (HiddenPhys)

summary: Gives API-only frozen models force sensing without demos or finetuning, on a Franka FR3 with no wrist F/T sensor. Real robot: GPT-6 Astra goes from 2/60 without force to 54/60, GPT-6.1 Sol reaches 47/60. ForceBench: Astra and Sol 87.5% (Fable 75.0%) vs 35.31% for the best trained policy; HiddenPhys: Astra 87/140 → 135/140, matching the hand-written expert at 136/140.
caveats: Authors: 'Model queries add seconds between primitives and preclude reactive coordination, a fixed menu limits new motion laws, and our ablations run only in simulation.' Primitive menu, physics estimators and per-task instructions are hand-written; ForceBench tools were tuned on 8 of 10 seeds; HiddenPhys gives object poses as noisy text (privileged state). Code to be released on publication.

name: RoboTeam
title: RoboTeam: Benchmarking Vision-Based Multi-Agent Control of Many Robot Arms in Real Time
interface: Coding agents (single, hierarchical, decentralized, or adaptive forking) call one robot tool (observe, straight-line/joint moves, gripper, delegate) and write their own vision code; MuJoCo runs in real time and never pauses
trials: 36 tasks (4 types × 3 team sizes × 3 levels), 4–16 arms, one run per condition

speed.latency: median task takes gpt-6.1-sol 3.5 hours
speed.cost: 218 million input tokens per median task (gpt-6.1-sol)

summary: Agents control 4 to 16 arms in real time from camera images only, with no ground-truth positions. With the adaptive system, gpt-6.1-sol and opus-5.5 complete 28 and 27 of 36 tasks and four other models at most 3, but a third of steps fail at least once and must be retried. Hierarchical/decentralized systems are faster but use up to 1.9× the tokens; 'no model or system is yet fast, cheap, and reliable at once'.
caveats: Authors: simulation only; 36 tasks are variants of four task types; each condition ran once, 'so differences such as 28 versus 29 tasks are not reliable'. Benchmark and records to be released.

name: PhysEvo
title: PhysEvo: Astra Can Act, Let It
interface: Task agent issues joint-level control_arms calls (12 joint targets + 2 grippers) or observation/geometry tools; a meta-agent on the same model revises tools, skills and diagnostic code between episodes
trials: 42 RoboDojo tasks × 5 held-out layouts; real: 5 tasks × 5 trials on AgileX PiPER
summary: Physical recursive self-improvement around one frozen model, with no weight updates or trained action policy. On 42 RoboDojo tasks: 68.14/100 score and 62.00% success on held-out layouts, vs 47.17% for RoboDawn's one-shot Astra agent. On 8 tasks challenging for direct Astra: 55.00% vs 1.25%. Real AgileX PiPER: 90.60/100 and 84.00% success across 25 trials on five tasks.
caveats: Each task keeps its own deployment version and task-specific skills; real-world runs continue skill revision between attempts. Baselines are taken from leaderboards and reports, not rerun. No latency or cost reported.

name: Push-T, revisited
title: Revisiting the "Push-T" Robot Manipulation Task with Agentic Robotics
interface: Coding agent writes, runs and revises a state-machine / MPC controller and vision pipeline offline in simulation; the generated code is the runtime policy (no LLM in the 10 Hz loop)
trials: Push-T: 200 seeds; Push-A–Z: 25 episodes per letter (650)

speed.cost: about 9.5 million output tokens, approximately $1,500–$2,000 API cost, approximately 221 hours in auto mode

summary: A demonstration-free code-as-policy for Push-T, built by Claude Code with Fable 5. The state controller reaches 100.0% success (vision controller 97.2%) vs 62.5% for the LeRobot Diffusion Policy checkpoint over 200 seeds, at 120.1 vs 223.7 mean steps. A self-generated curriculum extends it to Push-A–Z (99.4% overall) and to simulated Franka (vision 89.8%) and UR5e (vision 98.5%).
caveats: Authors: the agent may exploit simulator-specific state or contact behaviour unavailable on real robots; 'Claude is computationally expensive and sensitive to the prompt.' State controllers use privileged ground-truth state. Simulation only; development took ~221 h under human interaction.

name: EmbodyAgent
title: EmbodyAgent: Post-Training Embodied VLM Agents via Distillation, SFT, and RL
interface: Think-then-code through one execute_python tool exposing raw images/proprioception and 7-D end-effector control; no primitives, no action decoder
trials: 100 held-out test states (10 LIBERO Spatial tasks)

speed.latency: student median 136 s per episode incl. simulation; teacher 1,887 s of frontier-API inference per episode

summary: Distills a black-box frontier code-writing agent into an open 9B VLM via SFT, then online RL. Held-out success rises from 0/100 (base 9B VLM) to 14/100 after SFT and 84/100 after RL; median model calls per test episode drop from 36 to 11.
caveats: One simulated suite (ten LIBERO Spatial tasks), single run per stage, no real robot. The reported checkpoint is 'the best score observed' while monitoring the same test states, with RL still in progress.

name: Astra as visuo-tactile policy
title: GPT-6 Astra Is a Native Visuo-Tactile Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
interface: Scene + tactile RGB images and in-context demos in; ordered 7-D EEF-delta + gripper commands out, converted by a benchmark adapter
judged_by: simulator checker (official success criteria; one task's criterion relaxed)
trials: 19 tasks (UniVTAC + OpenViTac), 210 sampled scene seeds per setting

speed.latency: median response 15.4 s (vision) / 14.0 s (visuo-tactile)
speed.cost: 335.97 million tokens, CNY 7,505.05 for both phases

summary: First demonstration that a frontier model reads vision-based tactile images and uses contact cues, few-shot and closed loop. With visuo-tactile input Astra reaches 93.8% (UniVTAC) and 81.8% (OpenViTac), 22.9 and 13.1 points above the strongest reported specialist baselines; vision-only reaches 76.3% and 80.6%.
caveats: Authors: simulation only; cost limits most tasks to ten episodes instead of the full 100-episode evaluation, while baselines are published full-benchmark numbers. Uses task-specific successful demonstrations in context. Tactile input hurts on some tasks.

name: RoC
title: Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
interface: A trained task-state monitor triggers the agent only on events; the agent approves a prefix of the FastWAM action chunk, makes local EEF/gripper corrections, takes over directly, or revises the next subtask
trials: RMBench 9 tasks (30 trials/task vs agents, 100 vs policies); real SO-ARM101: 3 tasks × 10 trials

speed.latency: monitor 2.77 Hz overall
speed.cost: 288.3 tokens/episode vs 830.3 (GPT-as-Policy) and 1845.1 (Direct Control) on RMBench

summary: Event-triggered frontier-agent intervention over a world-action-model policy. On RMBench, 99.6% average success vs 75.6% for GPT-as-Policy and 71.9% for Direct Control, using 65.3% fewer tokens than GPT-as-Policy; 98.1% vs 83.0% for MemoryWAM, the strongest policy-only baseline. Real robot: 73.3% vs 30.0% for the policy alone.
caveats: Authors: failures are mostly difficult grasps that agent intervention can't rescue, 'highlighting agent capability as a remaining bottleneck'. Agent baselines use GPT-6 Astra while RoC uses GPT-6.1 Sol. The agent model on the real robot is not stated.

name: LEXP
title: Learning from Physical Experience:Context-Space Adaptation for Robotic Manipulation
interface: Actor emits absolute Cartesian pose / gripper tool calls per YAM arm with an intention note; a planner and an experience module write lessons back into its context; weights fixed
judged_by: human annotation against predefined completion criteria, independent of the actor's own declaration
trials: 12 real tasks × 3 trials per condition (36), bimanual YAM
summary: GPT-6 Astra as a direct bimanual policy that learns from physical experience in context. Across 12 real tasks LEXP reaches 23/36 (63.9%) vs 19/36 (52.8%) with memory alone and 2/36 (5.6%) for vanilla Astra. With memory only, Opus 5.5 gets 11/36 and Sol 5.6 0/36.
caveats: Authors: 'Bimanual coordination remains challenging, with no successful sweeping or towel-folding trials under any condition'; memory benefit is actor-dependent and varies across tasks. Three trials per task and condition. No latency or cost reported.

name: ReTrace
title: ReTrace: Cross-Stage Failure Attribution for Self-Improving Robotic Manipulation
interface: Executor predicts action chunks for a Franka; an Attributor on the same model traces failures to earlier decisions and consolidates validated corrections into a text skill
trials: 4 real tasks on Franka Research 3, 10 trials per task per configuration
summary: Self-improvement from autonomous physical interaction with no demos or weight updates; skills learned by Astra-high transfer to other models and effort levels. GPT-6 Astra-low improves from 0% to 80% on plug insertion and 0% to 100% on ball pouring; GPT-6 Sol-xhigh from 0% to 10% and 0% to 90%.
caveats: Authors: plug insertion remains difficult for Sol-xhigh even with the skill, so benefits vary across executing models. Who judges success, latency and cost are not stated.

name: LADDER
title: LADDER: A Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation Benchmark
interface: Compares VLM orchestrators sending text subgoals to frozen π0-like / π0.5 policies with tool-selection systems (CaP-X, GPT-Policy, PSP-Agent, TiPToP)
trials: 145 tasks, 3 suites, 2,024 simulated episodes per system; real: 12 episodes per task and system

speed.cost: per episode: GPT-Policy $4.02 vs $0.007–$0.17 for the others

summary: Scales horizon from 1 to 10 subgoals in the same scene. The low-level policy alone hits 85.4% on single-subgoal tasks but 11.0% overall. GPT-Policy on GPT-6 Astra is best on every suite (62.0% overall), then PSP-Agent (40.1%), versus at most 29.6% for learned-policy orchestration.
caveats: Authors: 'the simulation pauses while a system computes'; tool-selection systems get ground-truth depth and camera calibration in sim; 'High-level VLM inference is slow'. GPT-Policy was not run on the real robots. Tabletop pick-and-place only.

name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: a faster model for general purpose robotics
authors: Alex Gruenstein, Gabe Cohen, and the Gemini Robotics Team (blog)
interface: Plain-language goal + camera view; the model plans, writes and runs control code (Google Antigravity Robotics plugin, MuJoCo, Gemini API); can also drive arms directly from images. Low-level controller not described.

speed.latency: 'faster' (qualitative only)
speed.cost: 'lower cost per token' than Argon (no figure)

summary: A general-purpose fast Gemini 4 model that replaces Gemini Robotics ER 2 for embodied reasoning and ships a Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity (I2RT YAM, SO-ARM101, FR3 Duo, YAM Pro). On Artificial Analysis Robotics 0.1, 'Hydrogen scores 58', similar to Argon at a lower cost per token; a new arm is 'calibrated and ready for tasks in about 10 minutes'.
caveats: Vendor blog; no success rates, trial counts or latency figures. The AA score is Google-reported. Antigravity requires a paid Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription.

name: Claude Fable 5.2 (RoboDojo Sim)
title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
interface: Not described; RoboDojo controls a simulated two-arm robot from camera images, all models on the same Anthropic harness
summary: A general-purpose launch post that reports robot control 'even for robotics tasks on which it has never explicitly been trained'. 'At Max effort, Fable 5.2 scores 64.9%, more than double GPT-6 Astra (29.8%) and Fable 5.1 (27.6%)'; Opus 5.5 39.4%, Gemini 4 Argon (High effort) 34.2%. Claims it beat 'most AI systems built specifically to control robots'.
caveats: Vendor post: 'Scores are based on our internal runs for each model using the highest available effort level'; harness, latency and trial counts not disclosed; competitor models run by Anthropic. Real-robot videos (puzzle cube, bottle cap, drawing) have no success rates.

name: Mind2Act World
title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
interface: Agents issue pose-level motion-tool requests (IK / motion-planning service) from camera images and robot state; compared with fine-tuned VLAs (π0.5, X-VLA and others) and world-action models on the same tasks
judged_by: evaluator reading simulator state hidden from the systems
trials: 30 tasks × 3 levels × 2 scene settings; 900 episodes per agent

speed.latency: GPT-6 Astra 11.0 s per call; X-VLA 153 ms
speed.cost: GPT-6 Astra USD 25.13 per episode vs USD 1.12–1.24 for Gemini-4-Argon / DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

summary: Splits bimanual Isaac Sim tasks into Mind (history-based decisions), Act (precise timely execution) and Mind2Act (both, in closed loop). 'Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes'; X-VLA 'reaches 19.6% on Act, the highest among end-to-end policies'.
caveats: Authors: 'Simulation pauses during inference'; agents get an IK/motion-planning service and 'four times the physics budget of the end-to-end policies'; one fixed harness for all agents; sim only, one bimanual platform.

name: UniCraft
title: Alignment Drives Reuse: Learning Generalizable Robot-Use Agents from Heterogeneous Experience
org: The University of Sydney · Nanjing University
models: transfer: GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, MiniMax M3.1 Flash
interface: Agent in a Codex harness writes scripts against a shared skill / device-API package; a batch-level Reviser revises the shared skills and the orchestration policy from rollout feedback
trials: 2,700 learning rollouts per agent model; 5 rollouts per evaluation case
summary: One shared skill library refined across LIBERO-PRO, RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa365 (6 embodiments) with no demos or weight updates; pooled unseen success improves 'by 9-28 percentage points on LIBERO-PRO'. GPT-6 Astra reaches 86.00 on LIBERO-PRO unseen tasks (X-VLA 96.00). With frozen skills, zero-shot on RoboDojo: 'Overall success is 54.8%'.
caveats: Authors: different auxiliary tools across methods limit comparability; only high reasoning effort and 3 epochs assessed because of cost; RoboCasa composite tasks remain low; validated revisions can regress.

name: SO-101 Bench
title: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation
interface: LLM writes Python in the PyRUA-Lean code-as-policy harness (segmentation, 3D localization, IK) and can hand grasps to a sim-fine-tuned Galaxea 0.5 VLA; ablations also test direct tool calls
judged_by: simulator state (sim); operator under benchmark rules (real)
trials: 916 evaluation episodes; 60 paired episodes per ablation; 45 real layouts

speed.latency: median 197 s wall time to rollout stop for the agent (real)

summary: Isaac Lab digital twin of a low-cost SO-101 arm whose ranking of five policies (four VLAs and an LLM agent) matches the real robot (Spearman rho = 1.00). Across nine VLAs and WAMs 'the best learned policies score near 61%', while 'GPT-6.1 Sol writing code in the PyRUA-Lean harness and handing grasps to Galaxea 0.5 scores 83.2' (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017: 66.8). With the hand-off, GPT-6.1 Sol 'reaches 85% (51/60)', Gemini 4 Argon 77%, DeepSeek 65%, MiMo 55%.
caveats: The simulator pauses while the language model computes; simulation 'overestimates every policy's success by 9 to 31 percentage points'; learned policies share a fixed fine-tuning budget; one real environment; single arm, rigid objects.

name: Real2Gym
title: Real2Gym: Building Gyms from Videos, Bringing Skills to Robots
org: Shanghai AI Lab · SJTU · Zhejiang U · USTC · CUHK · HKU
models: baselines: GPT-6 Astra Direct Mode, GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh
interface: Agent writes an executable program per manipulation stage over segmentation, grasp-proposal and arm-control APIs; skills distilled from successes and failures guide later runs; sim and real share the interface
judged_by: predefined completion criteria and human inspection
trials: 24 reconstructed MuJoCo environments; real: 4 Franka tasks × 3 trials

speed.cost: Tokens (M) DROID/EgoDex: with skills 0.51/0.49 vs GPT-6 Astra Direct 1.42/2.56

summary: Turns human and robot demo videos into physics-validated sim gyms where a GPT-6 Astra code agent practises and accumulates skills, with no weight updates. 'outperforming GPT-6 Astra Direct Mode by 16.7% in success rate with approximately 74.9% fewer policy-execution tokens' in sim, 'while exceeding it by 33.3% in physical robot execution success rate across four tasks on a real Franka robot.'
caveats: Authors: stage-level code 'lacks the local fine-grained reactivity required for highly constrained manipulation'; real tests only on Franka arms with parallel-jaw grippers, 3 trials per task; reconstruction fidelity is judged by GPT-6 Astra.

name: BiCICLe
title: Bimanual Robot Manipulation via Multi-Agent In-Context Learning
org: Sapienza University of Rome · TU Darmstadt
interface: Text-serialized object poses and few-shot demos in the prompt; a leader LLM agent predicts one arm's discretized end-effector keyframes, a follower agent predicts the other arm conditioned on the leader; executed keyframe by keyframe with re-observation
trials: 13 TWIN tasks × 3 seeds × 100 episodes; 3 real tasks × 10 trials

speed.latency: median 125.3s LLM wall time per episode (Lift Ball, GPT-5-mini)

summary: Off-the-shelf text LLMs control two arms through in-context learning with no fine-tuning. 'Evaluated on 13 tasks from the TWIN benchmark, BiCICLe achieves 70.5% average success rate, outperforming the best training-free baseline by 6.1 percentage points'; real bimanual Franka: 60.0% Lift Box, 40.0% Open Pot, 60.0% Cleanup.
caveats: Simulation uses ground-truth segmentation masks; the discrete keypose interface caps precision; bounded by context window and API latency.

name: InSight
title: InSight: Self-Guided Skill Acquisition via Steerable VLAs
interface: VLM segments demos into primitives, flags primitives the VLA lacks, drives single-axis controller motions to acquire them and checks success from images; successes are distilled into a primitive-steerable π0.5 that the VLM then sequences
judged_by: ground-truth state (sim); human against binary criteria (real); VLM filters acquisition rollouts
trials: 25 trials per method (real twist / pour / composition)
summary: A frontier VLM teaches a VLA new primitives. Acquired skills reach '92% twist and 96% pour success, compared with 32% and 16% for CaP-X' using the same VLM; composing both into a 14-primitive task reaches '80% end-to-end success vs. 4% for CaP-X'.
caveats: Authors: new-primitive execution restricted to single-axis motions; only successful rollouts are used; 'manual environment resets are still necessary in this work'.

name: NovaPlan
title: NovaPlan: Zero-Shot Long-Horizon Manipulation via Closed-Loop Video Language Planning
org: Robotics and AI Institute · CMU · Brown · UPenn · UIUC · Harvard
interface: GPT-5.2 decomposes the task, picks among candidate Wan2.2 / Veo3.1 video rollouts, verifies execution and proposes recovery (incl. fingertip poking); object flow or human-hand flow from the chosen video becomes robot trajectories
trials: 10 per task

speed.latency: about 40 s per macro-action planning; about 90 s per macro-action including execution

summary: Zero-shot, no task-specific training or demos, on a Franka Research 3. In Block Stacking NovaPlan 'succeeds in seven out of ten trials'; FMB assembly is shown as a qualitative boundary case.
caveats: Authors: tabletop rigid objects, single fixed camera, 10 trials per task; video models often fail to generate corrections; 'we give no formal safety guarantee and would not deploy NovaPlan unsupervised'.

name: STeP
title: STeP: Signal Temporal Logic for Precise Specifications for Action Generation with Vision Language Models
interface: GPT-5.4 (System 2) formalizes the instruction as a Signal Temporal Logic spec over a fixed predicate / skill library; RRT + MPC (System 1) enforces it; an online STL monitor recalls System 2 with a history log to replan
trials: LIBERO-Constrained: 49 task–constraint instances; replanning: 20 trials
summary: 'On LIBERO-PRO, STeP retains 54%-89% success across five of six evaluated perturbation settings', against 12%–26% for CaP-Agent0 (copied from CaP-X); on LIBERO-Constrained it reaches 80% safe success vs 14% for SmolVLA.
caveats: Authors: 'To resolve objects and their locations in LIBERO we read privileged simulator state'; a fixed predicate library limits generalization; LIBERO-PRO baselines are not re-run.

name: AquaCap
title: AquaCap: A Training-Free Underwater Embodied Agent with Code-as-Policy
org: Sun Yat-sen University · Dalian University of Technology
interface: Policy agent plans condition-aware stages; coding agent writes control programs over high-level ROV / arm APIs; failure-aware memory drives replanning and code revision
judged_by: task-specific success criterion (lift held, transport within distance)
trials: Sim: 20 Stonefish tasks; real: 10 grasping + 10 transport trials
summary: Closed-loop code-as-policy for an underwater ROV with no training, using only onboard camera images and robot state. 'AquaCap achieves an overall SR of 66.43%, outperforming U0 by 19.29 percentage points' in simulation; real ROV grasping and transport are demonstrated.
caveats: Authors: 'Execution efficiency, however, remains a key bottleneck'; controls the ROV only through high-level APIs, not thruster dynamics; real-world success is much lower than in sim.

name: ScaleVLA
title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
interface: Frozen 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash vision-language backbone feeds a trainable action DiT that emits action chunks
trials: LIBERO-PRO: 500 episodes per setting; real: 10 in-domain + 15 OOD

speed.latency: 216 ms median per action chunk on four H200 GPUs; 384 ms median round trip on the real robot

summary: Puts a frontier LLM inside a VLA instead of using it as an agent, framed against GPT-6 Astra control being 'slow and costly'. 'LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones'; real charger insertion improves 'from 4/10 to 9/10'.
caveats: Trained VLA, not frontier-model control; needs four H200s for inference. No head-to-head with an agentic frontier model on the same tasks.

name: CoEnv / CoEx
title: CoEnv: Code-Driven Exploration in Real-to-Sim Digital Twins for Multi-Arm Manipulation
org: USTC · CUHK-Shenzhen · Fudan · SJTU · Shanghai AI Lab et al.
interface: Claude Code writes a complete multi-arm program, runs it in a real-to-sim digital twin and refines it against privileged-state checks, checkpoint predicates and rendered views; verified joint trajectories are replayed on hardware after collision checks
judged_by: twin verifier (privileged state) during exploration; task milestones on the real robots
trials: 10 per agent per task, 5 real tasks
summary: On five real multi-arm tasks with up to three heterogeneous robots, 'CoEx reaches 70% average success, against 50% for the same system without the code agent'; a π0.5 policy fine-tuned on agent-generated rollouts is also reported.
caveats: Authors: 'Real-world execution is open-loop replay, so residual pose offsets remain a main source of failure'; programs query privileged simulator state; rigid objects, fixed bases, static scenes; evaluation is modest in scale.

name: RoboDojo-RC Tier 1
title: RoboDojo-RC Tier 1: real-world leaderboard of frontier models, agents and VLAs (Robocurve)
authors: Sravanthi Machcha, Achu Menon, Sabrina Zou, Tzu Kit Chan, Jay Chooi
interface: Inspect Robots agent policy: absolute end-effector poses through tools at 10 Hz; top + two wrist cameras and robot state; 40 model calls for LLMs, 3,600 control steps for VLAs
judged_by: human grader with a per-task progress rubric (not blinded)
trials: 6 tasks × 20 trials = 120 attempts per configuration

speed.latency: 0.8–32.1 min per attempt across systems

summary: Six adapted RoboDojo real-world tasks on bimanual I2RT YAM arms, with frontier LLMs, a full agent system and learned VLAs/WAMs scored on one rig. Leaderboard: Waddle-1 81.4%, GPT-6.2 Astra (high) 65.7%, Dream-1 59.5%, Fable 5.2 (high) 57.5%, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) 54.5% … MolmoAct2 19.5%, GR00T N1.7 9.5%. Also reports cost and wall-clock time per attempt.
caveats: Graders knew which model was running ('grading is open to unconscious bias'); tasks are 'the six easiest tasks with the highest scores' on GPT-6 Astra; objects reset by hand; not comparable with original RoboDojo. Call caps differ by system type.

summary: Announced on X as Waddle Labs' first robot-use agent, controlling bimanual robots zero-shot on unseen tasks. Robocurve measures it at 81.4% on RoboDojo-RC Tier 1, the top score, ahead of GPT-6.2 Astra (65.7%) and the Dream-1 world action model (59.5%). A System 2 over System 1 design: 'agents that combine the capability of reasoning models and the efficiency of reactive policies'.
caveats: Robocurve: a 'full system' with 'one chat per task, a 10-minute limit and no call cap', while single LLMs get 40 model calls, so not like-for-like. LLMs and the lower-level policy type are not disclosed; no paper. Preview API by request.
